intended_object: The admissible finite quotients of the abstract free product ∗ᵢ Gᵢ of a family of profinite groups. These are the finite-index normal subgroups N whose preimage under each factor inclusion Gᵢ → ∗ᵢ Gᵢ is open in Gᵢ, i.e. the composite Gᵢ → (∗ᵢ Gᵢ)/N is continuous. The free profinite product is the completion of the free product with respect to these subgroups. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the use in `finiteGrpDiagram`/`product`.
explanation:
The structure bundles a `FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup` of `Monoid.CoprodI` (the abstract free product of the underlying groups). It adds the condition that, for every i, the preimage of the subgroup under `Monoid.CoprodI.of : G i →* Abstract G` is open in G i.

The quotient by N is finite and discrete. So the restriction Gᵢ → (∗Gᵢ)/N is continuous exactly when its kernel, the preimage of N, is open: a subgroup with finite-index-or-open... more precisely, the homomorphism is continuous iff the kernel is open, because the fibres are cosets of the kernel. The docstring says this equivalence explicitly.

This is the standard family of normal subgroups used to build the free profinite product, i.e. the coproduct in profinite groups (Ribes–Zalesskii). The library's `product` takes the limit over this family, and its universal property (`lift`) holds for an arbitrary index type.

The setting is already general: an arbitrary index type and arbitrary profinite factors. The degenerate cases behave correctly. The whole group (⊤) is always admissible, and an empty family gives the trivial group. Mathlib has no free profinite product and no equivalent notion of admissible quotient.
